title: Hameroff's view of microtubules and anesthesia as the switch for consciousness

tellings.quote: when you turn the microtubules off with anesthesia the rest of the brain functions completely normally it's only the microtubules that shut off and the person becomes unconscious
Hammer off is this anesthesiologist who realizes that when you shut down the microtubules the rest of the body is running as if it's totally alive but Consciousness shuts down
tellings.difference: Names Hameroff as an anesthesiologist and credits Penrose's book The Emperor's New Mind.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Hameroff's observation that anesthesia shuts down microtubules and consciousness while the rest of the body keeps working.

plain: An anesthesiologist named Stuart Hameroff noticed that when anesthesia shuts down microtubules, the tiny tube-like structures inside cells, the rest of the brain and body keep working normally but the person loses consciousness. Michels tells this himself in two episodes, tying it to a book by the writer Roger Penrose called The Emperor's New Mind. He raises it because, if true, it would point to microtubules as the place where consciousness is switched on and off.
